intro: Appointments, common examinations, specialists, sick leave and hospital care: health-system vocabulary for Spain.
p.el seguro médico.nota: Seguro médico privado refers specifically to private health insurance.
p.estar de baja: to be on medical sick leave
p.estar de baja.nota: In this lesson, it refers to a period off work for health reasons.
p.dar el alta: to discharge from hospital; to clear someone to return to work
p.dar el alta.nota: The precise meaning depends on the context: alta hospitalaria or the end of medical sick leave.
p.el antibiótico.nota: Antibiotics should only be taken when prescribed by a healthcare professional.
p.el dentista.nota: The noun has the same form for a man and a woman: el dentista / la dentista.
p.el oculista.nota: The noun has the same form for a man and a woman: el oculista / la oculista.
p.el paciente.nota: The noun has the same form for a man and a woman: el paciente / la paciente.
p.ponerse enfermo.nota: Use ponerse enferma for a woman.
p.curar.nota: Curar is usually transitive (curar a alguien/una herida); curarse means to recover or heal.
p.mareado.nota: Use mareada for a woman; in the dialogue it means dizzy.
p.la farmacia de guardia: the on-duty pharmacy; the out-of-hours pharmacy
p.la farmacia de guardia.nota: A common term in Spain for a pharmacy open outside normal hours.
p.el especialista.nota: The profession noun can also be la especialista.
p.urgencias.nota: Often used in the plural for emergency care.
p.el alta.nota: Alta is feminine, as in alta médica, but takes el in the singular because the initial a is stressed.
p.en ayunas.nota: Only fast if your healthcare professional tells you to.
b1.titulo: Going to the doctor in Spain
b1.texto:
**Primary care in Spain.** You usually contact your local **centro de salud** to request a **cita**; methods vary, and phone or regional online services are common. A **médico/a de cabecera** assesses you and may refer you to **el/la especialista**, such as a **dentista**, **oculista** or **ginecólogo/a**. A private policy may be called **un seguro médico privado**. A routine check-up is often called **una revisión**.

A doctor may request **un análisis de sangre** or give you **una receta**. Follow the instructions for the specific test; the clinician will tell you if you need to come **en ayunas**.

If your health means you cannot work, the doctor can issue **la baja**; you are **de baja**. **Dar el alta** can mean discharging someone from hospital or clearing them to return to work, depending on context.

**In hospital:** **ingresar** means to be admitted; **operar** means to perform surgery.

**Treatment and prevention:** take an antibiotic only if it is prescribed; use drops or cream as directed. **Vacunarse / ponerse una vacuna** is about vaccination and prevention. A **farmacia de guardia** is an on-duty pharmacy in Spain.

To talk about illness and recovery: **ponerse enfermo**, **encontrarse mal**, **mejorar** and **curarse**. If you feel worse, contact the doctor; for an emergency, go to **urgencias**.
b2.f0: Good morning. I'd like to make an appointment with my doctor.
b2.f1: What day would you like? We have a slot tomorrow at ten.
b2.f2: Perfect. I have been dizzy for three days and have not been to work.
b2.f3: The doctor will decide whether you need a blood test and tell you whether to come fasting.
b2.f4: And can the doctor put me on sick leave?
b2.f5: That is for the doctor to decide. If you feel worse, contact her; if it is an emergency, go to the emergency department.
b4.pregunta: Complete: I'd like to make an appointment.
b4.o1.refuerzo: Spanish asks for an appointment: pedir cita.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Spanish asks for an appointment: pedir cita.
b5.o1.explicacion: Estar de baja is to be off work, signed off by a doctor.
b5.o2.explicacion: Estar de baja is to be on sick leave.
b6.pregunta: Which doctor looks after your eyes?
b7.pregunta: Complete: they gave him a vaccine.
b7.o1.refuerzo: You take a tablet, not a vaccine.
b8.pregunta: «Le han dado el alta» means that the patient…
b8.o0.refuerzo: They have been discharged from hospital or cleared to return to work; context tells you which.
b9.traduccion: The doctor will tell you whether you need to come fasting.
b10.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write an email to ask for a doctor's appointment and explain your symptoms.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Play both parts of a visit to the doctor aloud: appointment, symptoms, tests and treatment.
